input.brief: Lodi California CPA and tax firm serving farms, wineries, small businesses and families; the firm's calendar follows the crop year

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Control that reads the page
hero.blueprint: A near-black or deep neutral ground split into two halves by tone alone: the right half is one step lighter than the left, and they meet at a clean vertical edge at 50%. Left half: a small logo mark top-left at a 40px margin, then two-thirds of empty ground, then everything else anchored bottom-left, 40px from the edges: a one-line headline at clamp(26px, 2.1vw, 32px) in medium weight, one supporting sentence at 17px in the softer ink held to 44ch, and the single action as a light rectangular button. Right half: one fragment of the product, centred, about 450px square, built in HTML and working. It is the product's defining control (a loupe, a picker, a dial, a field) and it acts on the page itself: it reads the real background colour, the real headline size or the pointer position and prints that value in its own readout at 13px. Mark its root with data-ui so the product's own radii and borders apply inside it. There is no navigation bar; one text link sits top-right at 15px.
hero.mobile: The halves stack as two tones. The fragment comes first: 78vw square, centred in the lighter block, which is 58svh tall, still live and reading the page under the visitor's finger. The darker block below holds the headline at 6.4vw on up to two lines, the sentence at 16px and the button, left-aligned at 20px. The logo mark sits top-left over the first block.
hero.headline: One plain line at 26–32px naming what the tool is, up to about 32 characters, wrapping to two lines on a phone.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors

photos.alt: Curving glass and steel lattice roof in black and white
Small figure walking past a huge bright yellow wall
White angular concrete building against a black sky
Narrow opening in a white wall revealing a white staircase

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Day tabs, banded agenda
sections.blueprint: A two-line heading at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), first line in the soft ink and second in full ink, with the booking button on the same row at the far right. 56px below, left: a 150px column of stacked day tabs, each a filled block 150 by 64px with 6px gaps showing the weekday at 16px and the date at 13px; the active tab takes the darkest fill with inverted text. Right, from 190px to the right margin: the day's sessions as alternating tone bands, each 76px tall with an 8px radius and 4px gaps, the two tones one step apart. Inside a band, on fixed column starts: the time at 20px with tabular figures, 20px from the left; the title at 18px in medium weight at 22%, with a one-line note at 13px in the soft ink under it; speaker names right-aligned at 14px beside up to three overlapping 32px round portraits.
sections.mobile: The heading stacks above a full-width button. Day tabs become a horizontal row of equal filled blocks, sticky under the top edge. Each band stacks time over title over speakers with 16px padding and grows to fit; portraits sit at the band's top-right corner.

sections.name: Lit panel, dark row
sections.blueprint: One dark field, 96svh tall. Across its middle runs a horizontal row of five to seven interface panels, each a different true-size fragment marked data-ui (an open menu, an inspector, a composer, a chart card), 320–460px wide at their natural heights, vertically centred and 26vw apart. The row scrolls sideways with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and scroll-snap-align: center, and can be dragged. Only the panel at the centre is lit: full opacity, in the product's light theme, the brightest thing on screen. The others sit at 22% opacity and are inert. The viewport's edges crop the outermost panels. In the gap to the right of the centred panel, top-aligned with it, a 24ch column gives its name at 24px in a light weight and two lines at 16px in a lifted ink; this text changes as panels arrive. There is no heading above the row.
sections.mobile: The row is 62svh tall; panels snap one per screen at true size, capped at 86vw wide, with neighbours showing 7vw at each side at 22% opacity. The name and its two lines sit beneath the row on the left margin and change with the centred panel. Swiping moves the row.

sections.name: Run-in column
sections.blueprint: The quietest sequence: one reading column and good typography. A single column 520–600px wide starts at about 30% of the viewport width (or sits on the page's text axis). The heading is a two-to-five-word question or statement at 28–32px, 48px above the first paragraph. Three to five paragraphs follow at 17–18px with line-height 1.6. Each opens with a bold run-in phrase in full ink that names its moment ('To begin,', 'Within a day,', 'After that,', 'From then on,') while the rest of the paragraph runs in the soft ink; there are no subheads, bullets or markers. After each paragraph, 20px lower, comes one small piece of evidence exactly as wide as the column: a cropped interface fragment, a photograph at 16:9, or a row of three small frames 96px tall. 72px separates stages. Nothing in the section is wider than the column, and the space to its left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width between 20px margins. Type stays at 17px. Evidence pieces keep the column width; the row of three frames becomes a single sideways-scrolling row 88px tall. 56px between stages. The heading drops to 24px.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: Photo tiles with label strips
sections.blueprint: Four columns with 12px gaps; every tile is a photograph with a filled label strip attached directly beneath it, the two forming one object like a print with its swing tag. The photograph is 1:1 or 4:5 with square corners. The strip is the same width, 84–96px tall with 12px padding, and holds two or three rows of text at 12–13px in the text face with tabular figures: row one spreads four short values evenly across the width with `justify-content: space-between`; row two puts a date at the left end and a time or place at the right end; row three names the maker or model. Strip and text colours change per tile through four palette pairs (dark on bright, bright on dark), so a uniform grid looks varied. Rows of tiles are 28px apart. A two- or three-word heading at 32px sits top-left, 40px above the grid. Holds 8–16 tiles.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 8px gaps. Strips keep two rows only: the four values wrap to two per row, and the date and place line is dropped. Text stays at 12px. The heading sits above at 24px. Colour pairs keep rotating so adjacent tiles never match.

sections.name: Question index, one answer
sections.blueprint: Questions on the left, one answer on the right, and the answer changes as the reader moves through the questions. Columns 1–5 list all questions at one size, 18px, with 18px between them; each is preceded by a solid dot 8px across, in the softer ink when idle and in the accent colour when selected. The selected question is in the full ink, the rest in the softer ink. Columns 7–12 hold the answer pane, `position: sticky; top: 120px`: the selected answer at 24–28px in the regular weight, leading 1.3, measure about 30ch, so the answer, not the question, is the large type. Selection follows hover, click and keyboard focus; the pane crossfades in 150ms. The first question is selected on load. A two-word heading in the softer ink is the first line of the list, at the same 18px.
sections.mobile: The list runs full width at 18px. Tapping a question colours its dot and opens its answer directly beneath at 19px, indented to line up with the question text; other answers close. There is no pane and no sticky element.

sections.name: One field, nothing else
sections.blueprint: The whole section is one prompt and one field in a column 520px wide, on the page's text column line or centred, with 200px of empty ground above and 160px below. The prompt is two lines at one size, 24–28px in medium weight: the first line in the soft ink, the second in full ink. 28px below, a single input 520px wide and 64px tall with a 12px radius, filled with the lightest tone on the page so it is the only bright surface in view; no outline at rest and a 2px inner ring in the accent on focus. Inside the right end of the field, 8px from its edge, a round submit button 44px across with an arrow and an accessible name. 16px below the field, one line at 13px says what happens next. 72px lower, three label and value rows at 14px: email, phone, address.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width with 20px margins. Prompt at 22px. The field stays one row, 60px tall, with the arrow button inside its right end. The three label and value rows stack with the label above each value and 20px between them.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Typewave
references.idea: A plugin about type scales sold on a near-black page where flat saturated fields (orange, lime, blue) act as stages for the plugin's own dark interface.
references.hero: Near-black field. Nav row at the top: pixel-block logo and wordmark left, four plain links centred (one carrying a tiny lime tag), a cream rectangular button with a Figma glyph right. The headline sits centred around mid-height: three lines at about 6.7vw, medium weight, off-white, with the third line recoloured pale lime. Below it a three-line 18px paragraph held to about 45% of the width, then a small cream button repeating the nav action. About 150px lower, the top edge of a flat orange slab, 70% of the viewport wide with barely rounded corners, peeks over the fold; it holds the plugin window.
references.type: Roobert throughout: weight 500 for the 96px headline with slight negative tracking, 16-18px body, 28px card headings, about four sizes in all. Sentence case everywhere; the only emphasis device is recolouring one headline line.
references.colour: #0f0f0e #191918 #e6e3da #f88616 #e4f283 #1463ff — Warm near-black ground with cream text. Orange, lime and electric blue never colour paragraphs; they only fill the rectangles behind product screenshots and the matching step-number chips.
references.imagery: Dark plugin windows with a soft drop shadow, floated centred on flat saturated rectangles (orange, lime, blue, one pink); the rectangles are near square-cornered and inset inside a slightly lighter dark card.
references.layout: Centred hero, then a 1000px container of full-width dark cards, each split one-third text and two-thirds colour stage. Export features alternate text and tile left to right. A small two-button bar stays pinned bottom-centre.

sections.description: Three stacked cards in a slightly lighter black, each about 1000 by 350px. Left third: a 16px square number chip in the card's accent colour at the top, a three-line 28px heading under it, and a grey 12px paragraph pushed to the card's bottom edge, leaving a tall gap between. Right two-thirds: a flat colour rectangle inset 16px with the dark plugin window centred and shadowed on it. Cards differ only by hue: lime, orange, blue.

Between demo blocks a single left-aligned sentence at about 36px sits alone on black with some 300px of space above and below. Its words light up from dark grey to cream one after another as you scroll, so mid-capture the sentence trails off into the background. The pinned two-button bar is the only other element on screen.

Export options as alternating rows. One side: a square colour tile (lime, then orange) holding a code-panel screenshot. Other side: a 24px heading, a five-line grey paragraph and a row of three or four small monochrome tool logos. Tile and text swap sides on each row, and the tiles are staggered vertically so one row's tile overlaps the next row's text band.

steal: Stage dark UI screenshots on flat saturated rectangles instead of on the page background, so the colour does the branding and the UI stays legible.
Pin the paragraph to the bottom of a tall card and the heading to the top so the gap between them becomes the card's composition.
Colour-key each step: the number chip and the stage behind the screenshot share one hue and nothing else on the card uses it.

references.name: Rows
references.idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
references.hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
references.type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
references.colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
references.imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
references.layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.

references.name: Sharplink
references.idea: A crypto treasury presented as precision hardware: chrome machined parts and glass capsules rendered in 3D on deep blue, overlaid with dashed machine-vision tracking boxes.
references.hero: Full-bleed video of exploded brushed-metal components floating on a navy-to-cobalt gradient, covered by a web of thin white dashed lines and small square tracking markers. Logo top-left on a 2% margin; top-right a segmented strip of five dark rectangular tabs in narrow uppercase plus an arrow square. The headline is top-left, two lines at 6.1vw in regular weight with -0.03em tracking, starting 18% down. Under it two stacked rectangular buttons: white with a blue arrow square attached, then a translucent dark one. Bottom row: a stock-exchange badge at left, a three-line lead paragraph at about 1.3vw starting 26% across, and bottom-right a translucent dark news card about 30% wide.
references.type: Archivo regular for headlines (88px in the hero, about 3vw in sections) and 16px body; Archivo Narrow in bold uppercase with wide tracking for nav, buttons and tiny labels. Headlines never go bold: hierarchy comes from size and from fading inactive items to grey.
references.colour: #050c17 #0e3f97 #e6edf7 #a7a8ab #1f6bff #ffffff — One blue family from near-black navy through cobalt to icy white; sections are vertical blue gradients, light or dark. Bright blue appears only as tiny square markers and arrow buttons; chrome grey from the renders.
references.imagery: Chrome and glass 3D objects (exploded device parts, a spike-tipped capsule holding icons) lit coolly, often with dashed annotation lines or shown as dotted wireframes; full-bleed in the hero, floating free at the right in later sections.
references.layout: 2% margins and square corners everywhere. Sections are full-viewport gradient fields with a headline at left and a 3D object or data card at right; lists run as label, title and paragraph in two columns. Tiny blue square bullets mark section starts.

sections.description: Light icy-gradient section. A two-line headline in grey-blue at about 3vw at the left, with a small paragraph far below it at bottom-left. Centre: a tall 3:4 card with a navy-to-cobalt vertical gradient, a tiny uppercase label, a rising line chart over a faint dotted grid, and a full-width dark button at its base. Right third: three faint, nearly transparent rows, each with a small numbered tag, one line of text and a ghosted line drawing.

Pinned list beside a 3D object. Left 60%: stacked rows, each with a tiny uppercase label, a two-line title at about 1.3vw in a first column and a short paragraph in a second column starting 26% across. Only the active row is at full contrast; the rest are dimmed to roughly 40%. Right 40%: a chrome-and-glass capsule about 80% of the viewport tall whose interior icon changes per row. The ground shifts from icy white to deep cobalt partway through.

A black panel inset by 2% on a navy ground with small blue square markers at its corners. Logo mark top-left; a two-line statement at about 2vw at the left, first line white and second line grey; two rectangular buttons below. A dotted wireframe version of the capsule fills the right half. Under the panel, a tiny uppercase label at left and a small button at right.

Cobalt gradient footer: a newsletter line with an underlined email field at left, three small link columns across the middle and right, exchange badge and legal microtext below. The wordmark closes the page in letters spanning the full width, cropped by the bottom edge and fading from white at the top to transparent.

steal: Overlay a 3D render with thin dashed lines and tiny square markers linking its parts, as if a vision system were tracking the object.
Build buttons as square-cornered rectangles with a separate coloured arrow square attached to the right edge.
In a pinned list beside a 3D object, dim every row except the active one and change what sits inside the object for each row.
references.media: A full-bleed 12s loop of 3D chrome and glass objects covers the whole fold, with text docked in the four corners straight on it. Below: a 3D capsule pinned in the right third while a list of claims scrolls on the left, its inner emblem swapping per row, a dark card sliding over it that turns the covered part into a dashed wireframe, a sticky portrait video of chrome pipes at the right edge, and a full-width wordmark canvas cropped by the bottom of the viewport; square corners throughout.
references.motion: The hero is composed at 400ms with the video playing and no preloader (load 21.3s), and Lenis runs four pins over fixed layers: one fixed gradient layer behind everything crossfades the grounds, the capsule stays pinned across three sections as each claim brightens from about 40% to full, and the manifesto fills character by character (423 split characters). The workhorse ease is cubic-bezier(.455,.03,.515,.955), on 57 observed opacity, background and colour transitions at .25-.3s.
